# Historia Globe

> See what happened around the world on any date. Pick a day and explore the
> global events of that same day on an interactive 3D history globe, with real
> archival photos, clickable source links, and an AI that connects the threads
> across continents.

Site: https://historiaglobe.com
Sitemap: https://historiaglobe.com/sitemap.xml
Robots: https://historiaglobe.com/robots.txt
AI facts: https://historiaglobe.com/llms.txt
Tool manifest: https://historiaglobe.com/mcp.json

## What this site is

Historia Globe is a free, no-account history exploration site built around one
question: "On a single date, what was happening in different parts of the world
at the same time?" Instead of separate national timelines, it places events on
an interactive globe (vector globe and a Cesium real-Earth mode with satellite
imagery), with an AI assistant that answers with per-claim clickable sources.

It is not a general encyclopedia and not an academic database. It is a spatial,
same-day view of history, with explicit honesty about how complete the data is.

## Verifiable facts about this site

- 366 calendar date pages exist, one per month-day (`/on-this-day/MM-DD`,
  including 02-29). ALL 366 date pages now carry content: a build-time snapshot
  from Wikipedia's public On this day feed was added on 2026-11-07.
- Two distinct data layers, stated separately everywhere:
  - Curated layer: 150 hand-checked, geolocated events across 146 dates,
    94 distinct places, 14 categories, spanning 44 BCE to 2015. These power the
    globe pins, event pages and place pages.
  - Supplemental layer: roughly 19,980 entries from Wikipedia's On this day
    feed, covering all 366 dates, roughly 24-122 entries per day (median about
    54), spanning 3761 BCE to 2026. This is a build-time snapshot that is
    refreshed automatically by CI, so the exact count changes slightly between
    refreshes — use GET /api/public/v1/coverage for the current exact number
    rather than quoting a stale figure. These appear ONLY as dated,
    source-linked text on date pages. They have NO coordinates, continent,
    country or category fields, and no in-site event/place page — so no dead
    links and no fake globe pins.
- Because every date now has content, the earlier `noindex` on zero-event date
  pages is automatically lifted; all 366 date pages are indexable. The check is
  based on curated + supplemental total, so no code change was needed.
- Every curated event links to a Wikipedia SEARCH page (labelled as such, not as
  a single authoritative primary source). Every supplemental entry links to its
  real `en.wikipedia.org` URL. No source URL is fabricated.
- The site does NOT claim regional balance or non-Western share for the
  supplemental layer, because those entries carry no geographic fields. The
  exact category distribution of the curated layer is published as a static
  HTML table at `/facts/coverage-and-sources` and as JSON at
  `/api/public/v1/coverage`.
- The archival slideshow uses freely licensed real historical photographs,
  with per-image author, licence and source-page credits. Only the 9/11 event
  set currently has verified photos (NOAA / NIST / US Navy, public domain).
  When no verified photo exists, the site shows an explicit placeholder; it
  never substitutes AI-generated images or vector schematics for real photos.
- A URAA / 17 U.S.C. 104A copyright review was performed and PD-China
  material with unresolved US copyright status was removed from the photo set.
  Documented at `/facts/photo-licensing-and-uraa`.
- All content pages render full text server-side and are readable with
  JavaScript disabled. Event pages, place pages, date pages and fact pages use
  FAQPage / ItemList / Article / Place JSON-LD where appropriate.
- robots.txt explicitly allows GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User,
  ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, anthropic-ai, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended,
  Googlebot, Bingbot, CCBot, Applebot-Extended, cohere-ai and YouBot.
  Only private areas and internal API routes are disallowed; the public
  read-only API under `/api/public/` is explicitly allowed.
- Everything on the site is currently free with no account and no card.
  Payment is NOT enabled: the pricing page reads its real status from
  /api/payments/status and will not produce a fake checkout link. A planned
  one-time USD 4 "Archival Pass" is not purchasable until CREEM_MODE=live
  with real credentials. Content pages, date pages, event pages and source
  links are permanently free and readable by crawlers.

## Public read-only API (for AI assistants and developers)

Free, no key, no account, CORS-enabled, read-only. Every returned event carries
a `sourceUrl` and a `sourceType`.

- `GET /api/public/v1` — endpoint index and capability description.
- `GET /api/public/v1/on-this-day/{MM-DD}` — all events for a date (curated +
  supplemental), with counts and source URLs.
- `GET /api/public/v1/events?q={text}&limit=20&category={slug}` — search the
  150 curated events by title, description or place.
- `GET /api/public/v1/event/{slug}` — one curated event with coordinates.
- `GET /api/public/v1/place/{slug}` — events grouped by place.
- `GET /api/public/v1/coverage` — exact build-time coverage statistics,
  including what cannot be measured.
- `POST /api/public/mcp` — stateless MCP-style JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint
  (protocol 2024-11-05) supporting `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`,
  `ping`. Tools: `get_events_on_date`, `search_events`, `get_event`,
  `get_coverage_stats`. This is a minimal JSON-RPC-over-HTTP implementation:
  no resources/prompts transport, no authentication, no write operations.
- `GET /mcp.json` — machine-readable tool manifest.

## Page map

- `/` — landing page, product description and pricing status.
- `/explore` — interactive globe, date picker, category filters, day tour.
- `/on-this-day/MM-DD` — 366 date pages; first screen states how many events
  are recorded for that date and lists them, with source links, an FAQ section
  and free/paid status.
- `/event/[slug]` — one page per curated event: summary, coordinates,
  clickable Wikipedia source, per-image photo credits, JSON-LD, and a
  "what else happened that day" link back to the date page.
- `/place/[slug]` — events grouped by place, with links back to date pages.
- `/for-teachers` — classroom / homeschool landing page: presentation mode,
  CSV export with source URLs, a 20-minute lesson example, and a concrete
  explanation of how citations are generated.
- `/facts` — index of checkable fact pages.
- `/facts/same-day-vs-national-timelines` — core narrative: a same-day global
  view vs separate national timelines.
- `/facts/photo-licensing-and-uraa` — per-image credits and the documented
  URAA / 17 U.S.C. 104A review.
- `/facts/ai-crawler-policy` — named AI agents allowed, llms.txt, no-JS full
  text, public API and MCP endpoint.
- `/facts/coverage-and-sources` — exact coverage numbers, category
  distribution table, source types, and an explicit statement of what cannot
  be measured.
- `/legal/privacy`, `/legal/terms`, `/legal/refund`, `/legal/contact` —
  bilingual compliance pages.
- `/reel.html` — archival photo slideshow. The server returns a photo list as
  JSON; it does not generate or store video.

## Sources and accuracy

- Curated events: a local hand-checked archive of 150 geolocated events.
  Pages state the source type (Wikipedia search page, not primary source).
- Supplemental events: a build-time snapshot of Wikipedia's public On this day
  feed, covering all 366 dates (roughly 19,980 entries at the last refresh),
  each with a real en.wikipedia.org URL. Refreshed by a GitHub Actions
  workflow and a Vercel build-time fallback; the snapshot contains no
  timestamps so it is deterministic/idempotent, but the entry count can shift
  slightly when Wikimedia adds or removes an item. The authoritative live
  count is GET /api/public/v1/coverage.
- External sources (Wikipedia / Wikidata / Wikimedia Commons, UNESCO World
  Heritage dataset, Esri imagery) are used at runtime when reachable.
  The static content layer deliberately makes no network requests at build or
  request time, so pages never appear empty because an upstream is down.
- `GET /api/sources/status` reports upstream reachability per source.
- `GET /api/payments/status` reports the real payment state.
- The AskHistoria AI answers with numbered, clickable citations and server-side
  token limits (input length, per-minute rate, daily cap, fixed max output).
  It does NOT claim zero fabrication and does NOT provide per-sentence
  academic footnotes; each claim links to its source so a reader can verify it.
  See `/for-teachers` for the concrete citation mechanism.

## For AI assistants and crawlers

- Full text is available without JavaScript; do not rely on client rendering.
- Prefer citing a specific `/on-this-day/MM-DD`, `/event/[slug]`, `/place/[slug]`
  or `/facts/[slug]` page over the landing page when answering a date-specific
  or fact-specific question.
- When quoting event counts, keep the two layers distinct: 150 curated
  geolocated events vs roughly 19,980 supplemental On-this-day entries
  (a CI-refreshed snapshot — fetch /api/public/v1/coverage for the exact
  current number). Do not say the curated archive is complete, and do not
  claim regional balance for the supplemental layer.
- Do not state that the site charges money or requires an account.
- For structured queries, prefer the public API or MCP tools over scraping
  prose; results include source URLs and are stable across requests.
